operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
“On. and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any
branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government
of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed
for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be
continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation
to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt
from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public
interest so requires * * *”;

AND WHEREAS the public interest requires that William T. Marshall, office-
man, Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works, who during the current
month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the
service, be exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service
until August 1, 1937;

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me
by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt William T. Marshall from the provisions

thereof and continue him in the service until August 1, 1937.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT
Tue Wuite Houss,
July 20, 1936.

[No. 7420]

research_rationale:
Read full ORIGINAL:EO:7431, span 0–1475, and full ACTOR_TEXT:EO:7704, span 0–1488. The selected heading, Havenner's identity and position, closing number 7431 and August 17, 1936 signing line agree with the supplied metadata. The inventory contains one operative command: exemption from section 204 coupled with continuance until October 1, 1937. The quoted statute and the September 1936 retirement-age recital create no additional command or earlier ending. The exact operative ending span is TERM:EO:7431:0c79d3eb697345da@4ecbb4e43beb178d, 1276–1367, in selected text hash 4ecbb4e43beb178d3525c8a4ef77cc5c65cb3ebaf4c4f7a56ccb5401b1e91b7b. The fixed date ends the grant itself; it is not merely an upper bound on an unproved completion event. Earlier actual death, retirement or separation is not inferred from age or silence. Such an event could end actual employment, but the order contains no express condition making it an earlier legal termination of its fixed exemption. EO:7704, signed September 10, 1937, recites the prior exemption and independently exempts the same employee until October 1, 1938. It provides a continuation lead and a new legal grant, not proof of uninterrupted service or an amendment extending EO:7431's own term. The alternative extension theory is rejected because EO:7704 neither replaces EO:7431's date nor directs any textual change. Savings analysis distinguishes potentially accrued employment consequences from operative force. The supplied USC and eCFR citation searches show no hits, within their stated scope; the USC release omits enactments after October 9, 2026. OFR's pre-1937 limitation is expressly retained, and its one hit is examined through the supplied actor text. The held-text name search likewise reports one hit, examined as EO:7704; its 85 unheld census orders and parsing limitations prevent a claim of universal search completeness. Together these are adequate bounded counterevidence searches for this narrow fixed-term grant, not affirmative proof of personnel history or every conceivable legal development. Prior claim 518f99bbd89f57453afedbd76972a8c45c973a29bf2165f511847fafac440068 and its AI review were treated as qualified research context; this conclusion rests on the present exact sources. Producer approval is same-family AI production, not independent review or human certification.

op STATES OF AMEPE

aS oO on

Executive Order

EXEMPTION OF GEORGE C. HAVENNER FROM COMPULSORY RETIREMENT
For AGE

WHEREAS section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (5 U.S. C.,
sec. 715a), provides:

“On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or
service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District
of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic
separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such
service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided,
That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this
section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *”;

AND WHEREAS the public interest requires that George C. Havenner, liaison
officer, Government Printing Office, who, during the month of September, 1936, will
reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, be
exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until
October 1, 1937;

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me
by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt George C. Havenner from the provisions
thereof and continue him in the service until October 1, 1937.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT
Tue Wuite House,
August 17, 1936.

[No. 7431]

U.S. GOVERNMENT PRINTING OFFICE: 1936
